To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the highest values of rCBV, Cho/Cr, Cho/NAA and LL ratio and 18F- FDG SUVmax were observed in CE regions.
the most malignant tumor area is characterized by the highest values of 18F-FGD SUVmax, rCBV, Cho/Cr, Cho/NAA ratio and LL ratio.
the combination of PET/CT, advanced MRI and histology, immunology and molecular genetics is the best approach to identify the most malignant areas in glioblastomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach for the identification of the most aggressive areas of GB, the extent of the infiltrating tumor and the sites giving rise to GSCs.
the development of a multimodal imaging approach to identify the most malignant tumor regions, to detect tumor infiltration, and to recognize the sites giving origin for GSCs.
the identification and characterization of the most malignant GB areas in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most malignant phenotype, the greatest spectrum of molecular abnormalities and the highest stem cell potential are associated with the CE area.

the combination of advanced MRI and 18FDG PET/CT, together with phenotype and genotype analysis, can provide an accurate in vivo assessment of tumor infiltration, the extent of malignant tumor areas and the sites giving rise to GSCs.

the combination of advanced MRI with 18F-FGD PET/CT is able to provide a detailed map of the most malignant areas, the extent and sites of infiltration and the most active sites for the origin of GB stem cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of MRI and PET/CT can provide a better understanding of the biological and genetic heterogeneity of the GB and can be useful to improve the treatment and the prognosis of this disease.

the combined PET/MRI imaging approach is able to identify in vivo areas of GB with the highest stem cell potential and the most malignant tumor phenotypes, as well as the sites giving origin of tumor infiltration.
18F-FGD PET/CT is more sensitive than conventional and advanced MRI for the detection of the most malignant tumor regions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
18F-FGD SUVmax, Cho/NAA and Cho/Cr ratio, rCBV and LL ratio can identify the most malignant tumor area, the extent of GB infiltration and the sites from which GSCs originate.

the combination of advanced imaging and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomographic/computed tomography can help to identify in vivo tumor regions with different molecular profiles and stem cell potential in GB.
the most aggressive tumor areas can be identified by a multimodal approach combining advanced MRI and 18-FDG PET/ CT.
